confidence_notes: I searched for food and drink prices once. The main source was crowd-sourced data from MyLifeElsewhere for Antigua Guatemala: cappuccino about USD 3.31, domestic pint about USD 3.85 and an inexpensive meal with a drink about USD 5.22. An older expat account from International Living gave lower prices, so I treated it as a lower bound. Antigua's tourist core costs more than these averages, so I set the inexpensive meal at USD 7.50, slightly above the crowd-sourced figure. The mid-range meal for two is my own estimate based on typical tourist-area restaurant prices. I estimated the cocktail and wine anchors from their usual price relationship to beer, not from a direct search. Imported wine costs relatively more in Guatemala. Accommodation anchors are general-knowledge estimates, not checked against live booking pages. The RBA rate came from a search summary that cited the RBA exchange-rates page and its RSS feed; I did not open the rba.gov.au page myself. Prices have been adjusted toward a July 2026 window.
comparable_city_reasoning: Antigua is a colonial tourist hub, so I compared it with similar Latin American destinations such as San Cristobal de las Casas and Oaxaca in Mexico and Granada in Nicaragua. The crowd-sourced source says Mexico City is about 23% more expensive than Antigua.
